note: Rewritten from the original description by Emerson (1928); the original is in English. The holotype is a soldier (Congo Museum, Tervueren); the description is based on a few soldiers and a few workers; the worker is not described separately and the alate is not recorded. The species is dedicated to the collector, Dr. J. Bequaert. Original collection record: in a gallery dug out of clay, in a narrow gallery-forest strip within savanna. Synonymy citations, distribution and figure numbers are not translated. Line-end hyphenation in the excerpt has been joined.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head large, reddish yellow; sides rounded, slightly narrowed anteriorly; a few setae scattered on the anterior part. Antennae 17-segmented, segment 3 shorter than segment 4, segment 4 shorter than segment 2. Compound eyes reduced to black dots behind the antennal bases. Mandibles black except near the base; dentition very similar to T. schmitzi, but the mandibles more slender. Anterior and posterior margins of the pronotum both concave. Measurements (mm): head with mandibles 6.21, head length to the tip of the labium 4.25, head width 2.89, antenna length 2.45, pronotum length 0.97, pronotum width 1.92, hind tibia length 2.27, left mandible length 1.84.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Closely related to T. schmitzi, but the sides of the head are more rounded and the mandibles more slender; T. rectanguloides is smaller; T. badius has a slightly wider head whose sides are more distinctly narrowed anteriorly; in T. monodon the head is proportionally wider and the mandibles are stouter.
